correctness.rationale: The invertible coordinate change yields exact collision exclusions; the quadratic-character census is uniform in odd q. The explicit quotient involution in arXiv:2306.01928v1, pp. 3-4, conjugates to its hyperelliptic partner when Δ is nonsquare, forcing odd Frobenius traces to vanish and producing an even genus-two Frobenius polynomial. Over F_{q²} the conjugate elliptic quotients have identical trace, giving the polynomial and an induced-isogeny class by Tate. A standalone exact-arithmetic verifier checks eleven prime-field censuses and fourteen quadratic-extension genus-two/elliptic point count comparisons, but is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2023 motivating work explicitly uses elliptic decompositions to find curves with unusually many points. The theorem identifies an entire, exactly sized smooth marked-parameter stratum—(q−1)(q−3)/2 curves—and proves no member can exceed q+1 ground-field points (indeed all odd extensions are trace-zero), while giving an executable elliptic reduction for every even extension. This is a natural completeness and search-pruning result, not merely a single toy example or a rewording of generic Weil restriction.
